config.baseline: unchanged guided-v2 request settings; its Spark locator is the shared Spark baseline
config.semantic_checkpoints: only preselected annotated frames with an actual tracker candidate

limitations: Experimental tracking support is not placement PASS and does not change the live placement checker.
Initial target and distractor identities are authored seed contracts. Runtime track identifiers do not independently prove object identity.
An evidence gap does not establish physical occlusion, absence, an identity switch or its cause.
Reacquisition requires distinct source-bound semantic views. Same-model agreement remains correlated and is not independent identity proof.
The caller must verify source bytes, frame extraction and model response bindings. This pure policy validates metadata consistency, not API origin.
Later ground-truth boxes and visibility labels belong only in separate scoring; runtime distractor boxes must be propagated model observations.
Reported confidence thresholds and overlap rules are authored development settings, not calibrated reliability guarantees.
Reviewed seed boxes are authored inputs, not automatic target localization or independent semantic identity proof.
A track ID may not establish identity across full occlusion, exit/re-entry, or long clips.
Missing frame/object records mean UNKNOWN, never verified absence; returned scores are not calibrated correctness probabilities.
The source SHA identifies the submitted clip bytes; frame indices and PTS identify decoded frames within that clip.
Reported costs use published video-frame rates and the 50-frame minimum, not the image-segmentation estimate; provider billing remains authoritative.
This experiment does not change live guided-v2 acceptance, verify physical execution or authorize actions.

New source episodes from exposed dataset families; a small development cohort, not an independent generalization benchmark.
These clips show partial occlusion and re-exposure; full disappearance and true identity switches are not established.
Tracking uses authored initial seeds; still baselines localize automatically. Initialization and compute differ.
Four methods score candidate visibility/localization at selected frames, not placement PASS or continuous procedural correctness.
The stronger semantic policy uses extra Spark calls. Report coverage beside unsupported support; abstention alone is not success.
Only sampled source frames are observed; unobserved intervals and hidden state remain unverified.
Reported costs are estimates, not provider-enforced spending limits. Same-model identity judgments remain correlated.
Descriptive scores on frozen selected frames, not a population reliability estimate.
Frames from a clip are correlated; separate clip IDs do not prove independent physical recordings.
UNKNOWN labels require withheld support. Unscored results are missing completions, not abstentions.
Coverage uses all labeled frames. Selective accuracy uses only supported predictions; zero denominators are null.
Correct support requires a positive label and target-box IoU at the frozen threshold; overlap does not independently prove identity.
Distractor alignment is only maximum box overlap with an authored distractor, not proof of an identity switch.
Selected-frame evidence does not establish visibility or motion between sampled frames and grants no physical-action authority.
